name: Tracegrid
tagline: A clearer handover for small manufacturing teams.
problem: Shift supervisors at small factories piece together incident notes from paper logs and chat messages, making recurring problems difficult to trace.
solution: A mobile-first shift log that connects incidents, assigned follow-ups, and the next supervisor's handover.
experience: The fictional founder spent four years managing shift operations at a component supplier.
validation: Founder-reported: 16 interviews with supervisors at 6 factories; 9 described missing follow-ups as a weekly problem. Three supervisors reviewed a clickable flow. No customer has committed to purchase.
uncertainty: Whether supervisors will consistently record incidents and whether owners will pay for a separate workflow tool.
nextMilestone: Test an offline-capable prototype over 4 weeks with 2 consenting factories; measure completed handovers and unresolved follow-ups.
budget: ₹6 lakh development, ₹3 lakh pilot support, ₹2 lakh field research, ₹1 lakh contingency.
lookingFor: Operator feedback and a conversation about prototype funding

updates.title: Simplified the shift handover
updates.body: Three walkthroughs suggested that a short unresolved-items list matters more than a dashboard. The prototype now opens on that list.

updates.title: Completed the first interview round
updates.body: Interview notes point to follow-up ownership as a recurring issue. Frequency and willingness to pay remain untested.

name: Stockloom
tagline: Know which material is actually available.
problem: Small textile processors lack a consistent view of material receipts, consumption, and stock reserved for customer orders.
solution: A lightweight receipt-to-production inventory workflow built around the records small processors already keep.
experience: The fictional founder is a supply-chain analyst with three years of textile-industry experience.
validation: Founder-reported: 12 interviews at 5 processing units and 4 workflow observations. Two owners said they would discuss a pilot after seeing a working prototype; these are expressions of interest, not contracts.
uncertainty: Data-entry effort, legacy spreadsheet integration, and whether operators can keep records current during busy shifts.
nextMilestone: Create a clickable workflow and test receiving and allocation tasks with 8 operators before selecting a build scope.
budget: ₹9 lakh initial development, ₹4 lakh onboarding research, ₹3 lakh integrations, ₹2 lakh contingency.
lookingFor: Textile operator introductions and stage-appropriate investor feedback

updates.title: Mapped the receiving workflow
updates.body: Four observations showed that receipts are logged differently at each unit. Standardising every field may be the wrong first step.

updates.title: Narrowed the first customer
updates.body: The initial focus is processors with one receiving point. Multi-site tracking is deferred until the basic workflow is understood.

name: Ledgerleaf
productStatus: Manual concierge experiment; no launched product
problem: Small accounting firms repeatedly chase clients for missing documents, with progress scattered across email, messages, and spreadsheets.
solution: A shared document checklist with clear ownership, reminders, and a completion trail. It is a workflow concept, not financial advice or a lending service.
experience: The fictional founder is an accountant who has worked with small-business clients for five years.
validation: Founder-reported: 14 interviews at 7 accounting firms. A manual checklist was used for 2 client accounts over one reporting cycle; users reported fewer status queries, but no controlled time-saving measurement exists.
uncertainty: Whether the workflow can reduce chasing without adding another channel, and how sensitive documents should be handled.
nextMilestone: Test a metadata-only prototype with 3 firms, measuring incomplete checklist items and follow-up effort without collecting live financial documents.
budget: ₹4 lakh prototype development, ₹2 lakh research, ₹1 lakh privacy review, ₹1 lakh contingency.
lookingFor: Accounting-firm feedback and a conversation about a small prototype budget

updates.title: Finished one manual reporting cycle
updates.body: Two accounts completed a shared checklist. The next experiment will measure follow-up effort rather than rely on perceived time savings.

updates.title: Reduced sensitive data in the concept
updates.body: The first software test will store checklist status and filenames only. Live financial documents are outside its scope.

name: Fieldnote
tagline: A shared view of collection-day exceptions.
problem: Produce collection teams reconcile quantity and quality exceptions through calls, delaying a shared understanding of what was collected.
solution: A simple offline collection log that records exceptions and syncs a daily summary for the operations team.
experience: The fictional founder has four seasons of collection-centre operations experience.
validation: Founder-reported: 11 interviews across 4 collection centres and 3 days observing collection records. A paper exception form was tried at one centre. No software usage or purchase commitments exist.
uncertainty: Device availability, offline reliability, seasonal adoption, and whether the organisation or centre should pay.
nextMilestone: Test the exception form at 2 centres through one collection cycle, then decide whether an offline mobile prototype is justified.
budget: ₹7 lakh development, ₹4 lakh field testing, ₹2 lakh device and connectivity support, ₹2 lakh contingency.
lookingFor: Agribusiness operators, customer access, and early-stage feedback

updates.title: Tried a paper exception log
updates.body: The first test suggests quantity disagreements need a separate record from ordinary receipts. It does not yet establish software demand.

updates.title: Added offline use to the hypothesis
updates.body: Field observations showed unreliable connectivity at the point of collection. The next test will examine what must work without a network.

name: Dispatchlane
tagline: Spot a delivery exception before the customer calls.
productStatus: Technical proof of concept; no production deployment
problem: Small fleet dispatchers identify route delays through manual check-ins, making customer updates inconsistent.
solution: An exception queue that combines dispatcher-entered events with existing route data to highlight deliveries needing attention.
experience: The fictional founder is a software engineer with three years building internal logistics tools.
validation: Founder-reported: 10 dispatcher interviews at 4 fleet operators. A local proof of concept processed synthetic route events. No live fleet data, claimed accuracy benchmark, or customer deployment exists.
uncertainty: Access to reliable route events, false-alert frequency, and whether integration costs exceed the value of earlier exception detection.
nextMilestone: Evaluate a sample-data integration with 2 operators and agree on an exception definition before any live pilot.
budget: ₹5 lakh prototype development, ₹2 lakh integration testing, ₹2 lakh operator research, ₹1 lakh contingency.
lookingFor: Fleet-operations feedback and an investor conversation about integration risk

updates.title: Processed synthetic route events
updates.body: The proof of concept can group predefined exceptions. Real-world signal quality and usefulness remain unknown.

updates.title: Made alert quality the first question
updates.body: Interviewees described too many notifications as a problem. The next test will measure relevant exceptions, not the number of alerts generated.

name: Benchpath
tagline: Make laboratory handoffs easier to trace.
productStatus: Clickable workflow prototype; no live lab use
problem: Small independent testing labs coordinate sample handoffs and report status through separate registers and messages.
solution: A status and handoff tracker for operations staff, with an explicit history of who moved a sample to the next step. The concept does not interpret clinical results.
experience: The fictional founder has a biomedical-engineering background and two years in lab operations.
validation: Founder-reported: 13 staff interviews at 5 labs and 6 walkthroughs of a clickable prototype. Staff identified two confusing status labels. No live samples or patient information were used.
uncertainty: Integration with existing laboratory systems, staff adoption, and whether operational records can remain separate from sensitive test data.
nextMilestone: Test 20 fictional sample handoffs with 6 operations staff; assess task completion and naming before considering a live-data pilot.
budget: ₹9 lakh development, ₹5 lakh integrations, ₹3 lakh workflow research, ₹2 lakh privacy review, ₹1 lakh contingency.
lookingFor: Laboratory operations expertise and early-stage review

updates.title: Revised two status labels
updates.body: Prototype walkthroughs exposed ambiguous handoff names. The next test will check whether staff can complete a sequence without help.

updates.title: Kept the first test free of patient data
updates.body: The prototype uses fictional sample identifiers and workflow metadata. A live pilot would need a separate privacy and integration review.
